title: Where a proposed polity's boundary would come from

route.description:
registered_source_feature: a source already in scripts/sources.yaml carries this exact feature. construct_from_registered: it can be built from registered features by union or difference. new_source_needed: a real boundary exists in the world but no registered source has it. none_available: no source is known to digitise this territory for this period.

registered_source_unfetched: the right source IS registered in scripts/sources.yaml but its file is not present locally, so no feature can be identified yet. ADDED because the enum forced a false choice: 20 Spanish units answered `registered_source_feature` naming mapspain-ign with an EMPTY feature_id, because data/geodata/mapspain-ign/provinces.gpkg does not exist here. That route asserts a specific feature IS the boundary, so without one it is an unverifiable claim; `new_source_needed` was also false, since the source needs fetching rather than registering. Use this instead, name the slug, and say in `reasoning` what has to be fetched and whether the licence has been checked.

source_slug.description: The scripts/sources.yaml slug, when the route uses a registered source.

feature_id.description: The identifier within that source, e.g. a GADM GID_1 such as JPN.1_1. Null when it must be constructed or does not exist.

licence_known.description: False when the licence has not been checked. A source cannot be adopted on an unchecked licence, so this must not be asserted true without evidence.

vintage_risk.description: How far the proposed feature's date sits from the polity's span, and what that costs. A present-day boundary standing in for a 19th-century territory is a stated approximation, not a silent one.
